question: Can two exact implementations of the same fixed-panel minimum-vote search improve measured time from available input arrays through final refit and prediction? Exploratory engineering experiment confined to the 14 previously inspected PMLB tasks and their 42 original outer folds.
fixed: Existing separating design and canonical context order, with the archived point and three bootstrap panels and exact stopping rule.
recent: Same model, masks, scores and proposal path. After the empty mask, check the most recent nonempty veto next.
recent_lazy: Same recent order. Batch the actual candidate and its reference into one prediction call if both were requested and are missing. Cache predictions and accuracy. Only if all four panels violate the accuracy tolerance may the implementation skip AUC/AP and emit four false votes. Otherwise compute missing full scores on demand. No speculative future predictions. Each arm uses the same XGBClassifier.predict_proba interface.
timing: Three independently refitted repetitions of all three arms in each fold. Permute the starting order deterministically with seed 331741 + task index*3 + fold; cyclically rotate that order with each repetition so all arms occupy every position. No common reference fit, imputation, gain anchor, search or final fit is reused across arms or repetitions. XGBoost and numerical libraries use one thread. The same selected logical CPU is used for every worker if process affinity is supported. The machine is shared. CPU and wall time measured from the beginning of converting already loaded feature/label arrays into prepared splits to the end of final prediction. File acquisition, importing, loading the in-memory raw table and saved split indices, score verification, disk writes and process launch are excluded. Time each stage separately; no pseudo-replicated significance tests.
verification: Every anchor, feature set, block proposal, acceptance bit and outer probability must reproduce the archived fixed-order result. For all actually visited contexts, compare every four-panel vector to the unoptimized oracle after timing. recent_lazy must use the identical sequence and four-panel results as recent, including rare-class AP using the original scorer when needed.
summary: Within each fold use the median of three repetitions for each arm. Report per-task three-fold averages and all-task means and medians, count task wins, distinct masks and predictor dispatches, avoided full metric evaluations, and paired absolute seconds. The prespecified engineering bar for general speed benefit on these tasks is a 5 percent reduction in the median of task-level full-pipeline time ratios versus BOTH fixed and recent, with a reduction on at least 8 tasks versus each. A search-stage saving alone does not meet this bar.
